<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Reviewing the current project state.

Install scripts already verify SHA256 before execution. The README still promotes dangerous one-liners without strong warnings. For s23, Pages serves install scripts from main HEAD while binaries come from releases, so channel documentation is needed. The README still lacks a documented trust model and preferred safe install method.

The preferred safe install path downloads the script from a pinned release asset, reviews it, then runs it. Alternatively, download the binary and SHA256SUMS directly and verify manually. The install scripts themselves pull binaries from GitHub Releases, so Pages HEAD drift is limited to the script itself.

Three options were weighed for s23: pinning Pages to release tags, documenting HEAD drift risk, or routing README installs through release assets. The chosen path hardens the README trust model and preferred safe install, updates release.yml to match safer documentation, and optionally strengthens the install scripts.

Pinning Pages to release tags is the cleaner choice for s23. This prevents install scripts from drifting from release assets. GPG signatures were considered but SHA256 checksum verification is sufficient per the acceptance criteria.

The concrete Pages deployment trigger will be `push: tags: v*` plus `workflow_dispatch`. This ensures install scripts on Pages stay locked to release assets.

Release notes will stop promoting pipe-to-shell as the primary install method. Install script headers will be updated to show preferred non-piped usage. Scripts will be hardened to fail clearly on errors. The README will gain a dedicated Trust model section stating that binaries are published only on tagged GitHub Releases with SHA256SUMS.

The README will use a three-tier channel table comparing Pages versus GitHub Release, plus a clear warning that piping remote scripts to a shell trusts the host at fetch time. Existing docs/ content is being checked for overlap.
</details></think>

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="run_terminal_command_v2"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **run_terminal_command_v2** • Run command: # Syntax-check install.ps1
$errs = $null
$null = [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path &#39;scripts\install.ps1&#39;), [ref]$null, [ref]$errs)
if ($errs) { $errs | ForEach-Object { $_.ToString() }; exit 1 } else { Write-Host &#39;install.ps1: parse OK&#39; }

# Checksum path smoke: fake asset + SHA256SUMS, run verify subset via pwsh
$tmp = Join-Path $env:TEMP (&#34;stepdown-checksum-&#34; + [guid]::NewGuid())
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $tmp | Out-Null
$asset = &#39;stepdown-rule-windows-x64.exe&#39;
$bin = Join-Path $tmp $asset
Set-Content -Path $bin -Value &#39;fake-binary-content&#39; -NoNewline
$hash = (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -Path $bin).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $tmp &#39;SHA256SUMS&#39;) -Value &#34;$hash  $asset&#34;
$expected = ($hash)
$actual = (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -Path $bin).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
if ($actual -ne $expected) { throw &#39;checksum smoke failed&#39; }
Write-Host &#34;checksum smoke OK ($actual)&#34;

# bash -n if available
$bash = Get-Command bash -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($bash) {
  bash -n scripts/install.sh
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }

```bash
$tmp = Join-Path $env:TEMP ("stepdown-checksum-" + [guid]::NewGuid())

$asset = 'stepdown-rule-windows-x64.exe'
$bin = Join-Path $tmp $asset
Set-Content -Path $bin -Value 'fake-binary-content' -NoNewline
$hash = (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -Path $bin).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $tmp 'SHA256SUMS') -Value "$hash  $asset"
$expected = ($hash)
$actual = (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -Path $bin).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
if ($actual -ne $expected) { throw 'checksum smoke failed' }
Write-Host "checksum smoke OK ($actual)"

# bash -n if available
$bash = Get-Command bash -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($bash) {
  bash -n scripts/install.sh
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
  Write-Host 'install.sh: bash -n OK'
} else {
  Write-Host 'bash not found; skip install.sh -n'
}

Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $tmp
```

````
# Stepdown Rule Analyzer

A TypeScript AST analyzer that enforces the stepdown rule for function organization in codebases. The stepdown rule organizes code from high-level concepts at the top to low-level implementation details at the bottom.

## Installation

### Trust model

- **Binaries** publish only on tagged GitHub Releases (`v*`) with `SHA256SUMS`.
- **Installers** (`install.sh` / `install.ps1`) download the Release asset and verify SHA256 **before** copying/executing the binary. Mismatch  abort.
- **Preferred path**: download the installer from a Release asset, inspect it, then run locally. That separates "fetch script" from "run script".
- **Pipe-to-shell** (`curl|bash`, `irm|iex`) executes remote content in one step - higher supply-chain risk. Use only if you accept trusting the URL host at fetch time.
- No GPG/cosign signatures yet; integrity is checksum-based against GitHub Release assets.

Channels (Release vs Pages): [docs/install-channels.md](docs/install-channels.md).

### From GitHub Releases (recommended)

Standalone binaries (~98 MiB, Bun runtime embedded - no Bun install required at runtime). Tagged releases publish linux/darwin (x64 + arm64) and windows-x64, plus installers and `SHA256SUMS`.

#### Preferred (download  inspect  run)

**Unix (macOS / Linux):**

```shell
curl -fsSL -o install.sh https://github.com/graffhyrum/stepdown-rule/releases/latest/download/install.sh
less install.sh   # review, then:
bash install.sh
```

**Windows (PowerShell):**

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://github.com/graffhyrum/stepdown-rule/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 -OutFile install.ps1
# review install.ps1, then:
powershell -File .\install.ps1
```

Pin a version: `VERSION=v0.2.0 bash install.sh` or `$env:VERSION = 'v0.2.0'; powershell -File .\install.ps1`.

#### Convenience pipe-to-shell (higher risk)

> Warning: pipes remote script straight into a shell. Prefer the download  inspect  run flow ab
````
